Outbreak of Viral Illness Disrupts Transportation Equipment Industry Workforce in Peru

LIMA – An outbreak of viral gastroenteritis has struck workers at several transportation equipment manufacturing sites in Peru’s coastal industrial corridor, leading to significant disruptions in plant operations and raising concerns over worker health and industry productivity.

The outbreak, which began late last week, has affected at least four major factories in the Callao and Chimbote regions, according to the National Association for Transportation Equipment Manufacturers (ANET). “We estimate that up to 18% of the workforce in affected facilities is currently on sick leave,” said ANET spokesperson Gabriela Ramos on Tuesday. “This has resulted in reduced output, with some assembly lines operating at less than half capacity.”

Local health authorities are working with company medical teams to contain the spread of the virus, which presents symptoms including severe stomach pain, vomiting, and fever. “We have intensified sanitation measures and implemented staggered shifts to minimize contact,” said Juan Estrella, human resources manager at Motran Equipos, one of the impacted firms. “Still, absenteeism remains high, and production targets are being revised downward.”

Union representatives have called for additional protective measures and paid sick leave for all affected employees. “The health and safety of our members must come first,” said Rosa Huamán, secretary of the National Transportation Equipment Workers Union. “We urge management to ensure adequate medical support and clear communication in this difficult period.”

Industry analysts warn that if the outbreak persists, the sector could face backlogs in equipment delivery and a prolonged period of reduced productivity. Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely and have not ruled out temporary site closures if infection rates rise further. The full impact on the industry’s workforce remains under assessment as the outbreak continues.
